 Election Day 2026: What’s open, closed in NYC on Tuesday?
 Updated: Oct. 30, 2026, 9:13 a.m. 
 | Published: Oct. 30, 2026, 9:09 a.m. 
 Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with some services and institutions operating on modified schedules. Staten Island Advance file 
 Set as Google Preferred Source 
 By Maria Vittoria Ravaioli | mravaioli@siadvance.com 
 STATEN ISLAND, N.Y. — Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and New Yorkers will head to the polls to cast their ballots in races for governor, Congress, the state Legislature and other offices. 
 Polling sites across New York City will be open from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. Voters who are in line by 9 p.m. will still be able to cast their ballots.
 Tuesday is also the deadline to postmark an early mail or absentee ballot. Voters can also return those ballots in person on Election Day.
 Election Day is not a federal holiday, but it is a state holiday in New York, meaning some government offices and services will be affected.
 Here’s a look at what’s open and closed on Election Day:
 Businesses, banks
 Most businesses and banks are expected to remain open on Election Day, though individual locations may operate on modified hours. Customers should check with a specific business or bank before heading out.
 Garbage collection
 There will be no trash, composting or recycling collection on Tuesday, Nov. 3, according to the New York City Department of Sanitation.
 Residents who normally receive Tuesday collection can place their material at the curb Tuesday evening for collection beginning Wednesday, Nov. 4.
 Mail delivery
 Election Day is not a federal holiday, so U.S. Postal Service locations are expected to be open and regular mail delivery will continue. UPS and FedEx also generally operate on Election Day.
 Transportation
 MTA buses and subways are expected to operate on a regular weekday schedule. The Staten Island Ferry is also expected to operate on its normal weekday schedule.
 Public libraries
 New York Public Library branches are expected to be open on Election Day and will operate on their regular schedule.
 Public schools

 New York City public schools will be closed to students for in-person learning on Election Day. Many campuses will be open as voting sites. Instead, schools will be in session remotely.
 Parking regulations and meters
 Alternate Side Parking regulations are suspended on Election Day. Parking meters and all other parking regulations remain in effect.
